summary: iOS 27 is Apple's iPhone software release for 2026. It was previewed at WWDC on 8 June 2026 and shipped to the public as a free update on 14 September 2026. Apple supports it on the same range of iPhones as iOS 26, from iPhone 11 and iPhone SE (2nd generation) up to the latest models.
highlights: Siri AI: a rebuilt, more conversational Siri with personal context, onscreen awareness and its own Siri app (English first, in beta)
Siri mode in the Camera app for asking about and acting on what the camera sees
New AI photo tools in Photos, including Spatial Reframing, Extend and an improved Clean Up
Expanded child-safety controls such as Ask to Browse in Safari, Time Allowances and a redesigned Screen Time
Performance work: Apple cites app launches up to 30% faster and photos loading up to 70% faster after capture
Liquid Glass refinements, including a setting to adjust transparency

summary: iOS 26 is Apple's iPhone software release for 2025. It was unveiled at WWDC on 9 June 2025 and released as a free update on 15 September 2025. It runs on iPhone 11 and later, plus iPhone SE (2nd generation and later); support for iPhone XS, XS Max and XR ended with this version.
highlights: Liquid Glass, a new translucent design language across controls, icons and widgets
Live Translation built into Messages, FaceTime and Phone
Visual intelligence that works on whatever is shown on the iPhone screen
Redesigned Phone app with Call Screening and Hold Assist
Messages updates: unknown-sender filtering, polls and custom chat backgrounds
New Apple Games app as a hub for the player's games

summary: iPadOS 27 is Apple's 2026 software release for iPad. It was previewed at WWDC on 8 June 2026 and became available as a free update on 14 September 2026. Apple's compatibility list starts at iPad Pro (4th generation), iPad Air (4th generation), iPad (9th generation) and iPad mini (6th generation), so several older iPads that run iPadOS 26 are not on it.
highlights: Siri AI with a dedicated Siri app; Siri AI and the new Apple Intelligence features need iPad mini (A17 Pro) or an iPad with M1 or later
Visual Intelligence for asking about and acting on onscreen content
Apple Intelligence additions in apps such as Photos editing, Notes, Safari tab grouping and Image Playground
Child-safety tools including Ask to Browse and Time Allowances and Schedules
Faster app launches and file transfers, plus Liquid Glass refinements
devices: iPad Pro (4th generation and later, M1 and later)
iPad Air (4th generation and later, M2 and later)
iPad mini (6th generation, A17 Pro and later)

summary: iPadOS 26 is Apple's 2025 software release for iPad. It was announced at WWDC on 9 June 2025 and released as a free update on 15 September 2025. Apple's support page lists iPads from the iPad (8th generation), iPad mini (5th generation), iPad Air (3rd generation) and early iPad Pro models onward; iPad (7th generation) is no longer supported.
highlights: A new windowing system for opening, arranging and switching between app windows
A menu bar with app commands at the top of the screen
Files app improvements and folders that can be pinned to the Dock
New Preview app for viewing and marking up PDFs
Background Tasks shown as Live Activities, and the Journal app on iPad
Liquid Glass design shared with iOS 26

summary: Android 17 is Google's 2026 Android release. The first beta came out on 13 February 2026 and the stable version started rolling out to supported Pixel devices on 16 June 2026. Google supports it on Pixel 6 and newer, and the Pixel 11 series ships with it.
highlights: Bubbles: any app can float over others, with a docked bubble bar on large screens
Screen Reactions toolbar for recording the selfie camera and the screen together
Temporary precise-location access and the option to share only selected contacts with apps
Find Hub 'Mark as lost' can lock a phone behind biometrics; stronger limits on PIN guessing
Continue On for picking up a task from the phone on a tablet
Stricter per-device app memory limits for smoother performance

summary: Android 16 is Google's 2025 Android release. The first developer preview appeared in November 2024 and the stable version reached supported Pixel phones on 10 June 2025, with other brands following later in the year. It is supported on Pixel 6 and newer, and the Pixel 10 series launched with it.
highlights: Live Updates notifications for real-time progress from ride-share and delivery apps
Automatic grouping of notifications from the same app
Better hearing-aid support, including using the phone's microphone on calls
Advanced Protection: one switch that turns on Google's strongest device security settings
Desktop-style windowing on tablets for resizing and arranging app windows

summary: One UI 9 is Samsung's Galaxy software based on Android 17. A beta opened for the Galaxy S26 series on 12 May 2026, the Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra, Z Fold8 and Z Flip8 launched with it, and the official update for the Galaxy S26 series began on 16 September 2026. Samsung says other Galaxy devices will follow gradually but has not yet published a full list.
highlights: Built on Android 17
My FanCam video mode that follows a chosen person
Now Brief gains generative, editable cards; Now Nudge suggestions for everyday tasks
Interpreter thread view, Document Scan improvements and structured Voice Recorder summaries
Security Brief and on-device Privacy Alerts; Scam Detection expanded to more countries
Warranty and Care section in Settings

summary: One UI 8.5 is an Android 16-based update to Samsung's Galaxy software. A beta began on 8 December 2025, the Galaxy S26 series shipped with it in early 2026, and the official rollout to earlier flagships started in Korea on 6 May 2026, with other markets after.
highlights: Photo Assist: keep editing a photo through several steps and review an edit history
Quick Share suggests sending a photo to the people recognised in it
Audio Broadcast via Auracast to nearby LE Audio devices (Galaxy S25, S25+ and S25 Ultra in the beta)
Storage Share: browse files from other Galaxy devices in My Files
Theft Protection additions, including a lock after repeated failed authentication

summary: One UI 8 is Samsung's Galaxy software based on Android 16. Samsung opened a beta on 28 May 2025, launched it on the Galaxy Z Fold7 and Z Flip7 in July 2025, and announced the official rollout for the Galaxy S25 series on 15 September 2025, followed by older Galaxy phones and tablets.
highlights: Built on Android 16
Now Bar and Now Brief personalised updates
Knox Enhanced Encrypted Protection and Secure Wi-Fi with post-quantum cryptography
Gemini Live and Circle to Search with on-screen translation
Audio Eraser, Portrait Studio, Call Captions and Interpreter
Galaxy AI improvements for large screens and multi-window

summary: HyperOS 4 is Xiaomi's newest system software for its Xiaomi, REDMI and POCO phones and tablets. Xiaomi's global schedule starts the rollout in early November 2026, continues in mid-November and finishes the listed devices in December 2026, with timing that can vary by market and model.
highlights: New 'soft light glass' visual style with light and shadow effects
Faster app and camera launches, with Xiaomi quoting gains over HyperOS 3 in its own tests
Lock screen styling, notification stacking, resizable home-screen folders and widget stacking
Xiaomi HyperAI tools: AI voice notes, speech recognition, translation of conversations and gallery search
Post-quantum encryption for key delivery in end-to-end encrypted channels
devices: POCO X8 Pro Iron Man Edition
POCO X7 Pro Iron Man Edition

summary: HyperOS 3 is the previous major version of Xiaomi's system software. Xiaomi rolled it out to global phones and tablets in three waves, between October 2025 and March 2026, starting with the Xiaomi 15 family.
highlights: HyperIsland: a persistent status view and floating window for supported apps
AI lock screen and AI dynamic wallpapers
Redesigned icons and widgets, plus a customisable Gallery layout
HyperAI writing, transcription, summaries, search and translation tools
HyperConnect: Touch to share with Apple devices and resizable app windows
Post-quantum encryption for key delivery and cross-device biometric unlock
devices: POCO X7 Pro Iron Man Edition

summary: OxygenOS 16 is the Android 16-based version of OnePlus's software. OnePlus presented it at a launch event on 16 October 2025 and rolls it out in batches that depend on model, country and carrier. OnePlus says its device list is not exhaustive.
highlights: Plus Mind with the Plus Key for saving and finding schedules, notes and voice memos
Mind Space integration with the Gemini app
Fluid Cloud live updates for sports, music, traffic and delivery apps
OnePlus Flow Motion animations and smoother multitasking
Open Canvas with up to five apps on OnePlus Pad 3 and Pad 2
O+ Connect for working with Mac, Windows PCs and iPhone

summary: Nothing OS 5.0 is Nothing's Android 17-era software for its Nothing and CMF phones. The open beta began on Phone (3) on 26 August 2026 and the general release started from 12 October 2026, with other models following over the next few months. Phone (1), Phone (2) and CMF Phone 1 do not get it.
highlights: Refreshed home screen with wallpaper-aware colours, tinted icons and transparent widgets
New Geist typeface and Gooey and Micrographics clock faces
Glyph Timer and a dedicated Glyph app
Away Time for tracking phone-free breaks and Collector photo stickers
Essential AI additions such as Smart Collections and real-time text in Essential Voice
